---
title: Export Formats
description: Export Oicana templates to PDF, SVG, and PNG.
---

import { Aside, Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Templates can be exported to PDF, SVG, and PNG.

## PDF export

The PDF export supports [all standards that Typst has to offer](https://typst.app/docs/reference/pdf/#pdf-standards). The default in Oicana is PDF/A-3b (PDF 1.7).

You can configure the default PDF standards to use when exporting a given template in the template's manifest file.

```toml
[tool.oicana.export.pdf]
standards = ["ua-1"]
```

The manifest above would configure this template to [produce PDF files for Universal Access](https://typst.app/docs/reference/pdf/#pdf-ua).

<Aside type="caution" title="Strict standards have prerequisites">
Strict standards require additional metadata in your template, including the default. PDF/A profiles need a document date. PDF/UA-1 needs a document title and language, plus alt text on every image and equation.

```typst
#set document(title: "Invoice 2026-001", date: datetime.today())
#set text(lang: "en")
```

Typst surfaces an error per missing detail (e.g. `PDF/A-3b error: missing document date`); see [Typst's PDF reference](https://typst.app/docs/reference/pdf/) for the full list of prerequisites for each standard.

[Template tests](/docs/templates/tests/#pdf-standards) export every test case with the standards from the manifest, so a missing prerequisite fails `oicana test` instead of your production export.
</Aside>

### Tagged PDFs

By default, Oicana produces tagged (accessible) PDFs. You can turn tagging off in the template's manifest:

```toml
[tool.oicana.export.pdf]
tagged = false
```

<Aside>
Oicana turns tagging off when you export only a subset of a document's pages, because Typst cannot tag partial exports. A template that declares `ua-1` is the exception: PDF/UA-1 requires tagging, so Typst tags the subset anyway.
</Aside>

### Combining standards

The `standards` array accepts three kinds of entries (see [the Typst docs for a complete list of supported standards](https://typst.app/docs/reference/pdf)):

- **Versions**: `1.4`, `1.5`, `1.6`, `1.7`, `2.0`
- **PDF/A profiles**: every `a-*` entry (e.g. `a-2b`, `a-3b`, `a-4`)
- **PDF/UA**: `ua-1`

You can list at most one of each kind, and they all have to share a compatible base PDF version. In particular, a PDF/A profile and PDF/UA-1 combine into an accessible, archivable document when both build on the same PDF version. For example, PDF/A-3b and PDF/UA-1 (both based on PDF 1.7):

```toml
[tool.oicana.export.pdf]
standards = ["ua-1", "a-3b"]
```

This is exactly the combination [our `invoice` example template](https://github.com/oicana/oicana-example-templates/tree/main/templates/invoice) exports, and what an accessible e-invoice needs.

Incompatible combinations are rejected. For example, `["a-4", "ua-1"]` fails because PDF/A-4 builds on PDF 2.0 while PDF/UA-1 requires PDF 1.7 or earlier. Listing two PDF/A profiles or two versions is rejected as well. `oicana validate` catches invalid combinations in your manifest, and `oicana test` catches documents that do not meet the standards they declare.

### Embedded files and e-invoices

Oicana's PDF export can attach files to the document and write custom XMP metadata. Together with the default PDF/A-3b standard, this is what e-invoice formats such as [ZUGFeRD and Factur-X](https://www.ferd-net.de/en/standards/zugferd/factur-x) require: a human-readable PDF/A-3b document with the structured invoice XML embedded as an associated file and the matching metadata declared in the document's XMP.

## PNG export

In many scenarios, PNG export is an easy option for previews.

Oicana integrations allow configuring the pixels per point in a PNG export. A smaller ratio leads to faster file generation and smaller files, but lower resolution. The default is 1px/pt. The parameter is called `pixelsPerPt` (`pixels_per_pt` in Python and Rust) and comes before the page range on every PNG export method, as in the examples below.

<Aside>
When a PNG export covers more than one page, the pages are merged into a single, vertically stacked image. Export pages individually (see below) if you need separate files.
</Aside>

<Aside>
Typst's PNG export is optimized for speed, not file size. Before you save the images or send them over the network, consider optimizing them.
</Aside>

To keep memory usage in check, a PNG export is limited to 256 million pixels by default, which is about 1 GB of memory. The budget covers the per-page buffers as well as the merged canvas they are combined into, so an export costs roughly twice its output pixels. That corresponds to roughly 14 A4 pages at 300 DPI, or a single A4 page at about 1150 DPI. A large document combined with a high pixels-per-point ratio can hit this limit. In that case you can still export pages individually.

## SVG export

Like PNG, a multi-page export produces a single file with the pages stacked vertically, separated by the same gap. A two-page A4 document comes out as one SVG with a `viewBox` covering both pages. Export pages individually (see below) if you need one file per page.

SVG has no resolution setting, since it is vector output, and none of the PNG pixel budget applies to it.

## Exporting specific pages

Every export method accepts an optional page range, so you can export just a part of a document instead of the whole thing. Page indices are **0-based and inclusive**: the range `0`–`2` exports the first three pages. Both bounds are optional. Omitting the start exports from the first page, omitting the end exports through the last page.

Each integration exposes this as a `pages` argument on the export methods, together with a `PageRange` helper to construct the range. Method names follow each language's conventions, for example `exportPdf` in Node.js, `export_pdf` in Python and Rust, and `ExportPdf` in C#.

<Tabs syncKey="integration">
  <TabItem label="TS (Browser)">
    ```typescript
    import { CompilationMode, PageRange, Template } from '@oicana/browser';

    // The first three pages
    const excerpt = template.exportPdf(
      jsonInputs,
      blobInputs,
      CompilationMode.Production,
      PageRange.of(0, 2),
    );

    // The third page through the end of the document
    const rest = template.exportPdf(
      jsonInputs,
      blobInputs,
      CompilationMode.Production,
      PageRange.of(2),
    );

    // The first page as a PNG at twice the default resolution
    const preview = template.exportPng(
      jsonInputs,
      blobInputs,
      CompilationMode.Production,
      2.0,
      PageRange.single(0),
    );
    ```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="C#">
    ```csharp
    using Oicana.Config;

    var options = new CompilationOptions(CompilationMode.Production);

    // The first three pages
    var excerpt = template.ExportPdf(jsonInputs, blobInputs, options, PageRange.Of(0, 2));

    // The third page through the end of the document
    var rest = template.ExportPdf(jsonInputs, blobInputs, options, PageRange.Of(2));

    // The first page as a PNG at twice the default resolution
    var preview = template.ExportPng(jsonInputs, blobInputs, options, 2.0f, PageRange.Single(0));
    ```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Java">
    ```java
    import com.oicana.CompilationMode;
    import com.oicana.PageRange;

    // The first three pages
    byte[] excerpt = template.exportPdf(
            jsonInputs, blobInputs, CompilationMode.PRODUCTION, PageRange.of(0, 2));

    // The third page through the end of the document
    byte[] rest = template.exportPdf(
            jsonInputs, blobInputs, CompilationMode.PRODUCTION, PageRange.of(2, null));

    // The first page as a PNG at twice the default resolution
    byte[] preview = template.exportPng(
            jsonInputs, blobInputs, CompilationMode.PRODUCTION, 2.0f, PageRange.single(0));
    ```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="TS (Node.js)">
    ```typescript
    import { CompilationMode, PageRange, Template } from '@oicana/node';

    // The first three pages
    const excerpt = template.exportPdf(
      jsonInputs,
      blobInputs,
      CompilationMode.Production,
      PageRange.of(0, 2),
    );

    // The third page through the end of the document
    const rest = template.exportPdf(
      jsonInputs,
      blobInputs,
      CompilationMode.Production,
      PageRange.of(2),
    );

    // The first page as a PNG at twice the default resolution
    const preview = template.exportPng(
      jsonInputs,
      blobInputs,
      CompilationMode.Production,
      2.0,
      PageRange.single(0),
    );
    ```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="PHP">
    ```php
    use Oicana\PageRange;

    // The first three pages
    $excerpt = $template->exportPdf(
        jsonInputs: $jsonInputs,
        pages: PageRange::of(0, 2),
    );

    // The third page through the end of the document
    $rest = $template->exportPdf(
        jsonInputs: $jsonInputs,
        pages: PageRange::of(2),
    );

    // The first page as a PNG at twice the default resolution
    $preview = $template->exportPng(
        jsonInputs: $jsonInputs,
        pixelsPerPt: 2.0,
        pages: PageRange::single(0),
    );
    ```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Python">
    ```python
    from oicana import PageRange

    # The first three pages
    excerpt = template.export_pdf(json_inputs=json_inputs, pages=PageRange.of(0, 2))

    # The third page through the end of the document
    rest = template.export_pdf(json_inputs=json_inputs, pages=PageRange.of(2))

    # The first page as a PNG at twice the default resolution
    preview = template.export_png(
        json_inputs=json_inputs,
        pixels_per_pt=2.0,
        pages=PageRange.single(0),
    )
    ```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Rust">
    ```rust
    use oicana::export::pages::PageRange;
    use oicana::export::pdf::export_pdf;
    use oicana::export::png::export_png;

    let result = template.compile(inputs)?;

    // The first three pages
    let excerpt = export_pdf(
        &result.document,
        &template,
        template.manifest().pdf_standards(),
        template.manifest().pdf_tagged(),
        Some(&PageRange { start: Some(0), end: Some(2) }),
    )?;

    // The third page through the end of the document
    let rest = export_pdf(
        &result.document,
        &template,
        template.manifest().pdf_standards(),
        template.manifest().pdf_tagged(),
        Some(&PageRange::from(2)),
    )?;

    // The first page as a PNG at twice the default resolution
    let preview = export_png(&result.document, 2.0, Some(&PageRange::single(0)))?;
    ```

    Rust builds a range with the `PageRange` struct or its `single`, `from` and `to` constructors, and passes `None` for the whole document.

    PNG and SVG export sit behind Cargo features:

    ```toml title="Part of Cargo.toml"
    oicana = { version = "0.8.0", features = ["png", "svg"] }
    ```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Reusing a compilation

The export methods above compile the template and export it in a single call. When you need several exports of the *same* inputs, for example a full PDF plus a per-page PNG preview, compiling once and exporting repeatedly avoids the redundant compilation work.

Call `compile` instead of an export method to get a compiled document handle. It exposes the same export methods and reports its page count, so you can export individual pages or page ranges without recompiling. Release the handle when you are done to free memory.

<Tabs syncKey="integration">
  <TabItem label="TS (Browser)">
    ```typescript
    import { PageRange, Template } from '@oicana/browser';

    const document = template.compile(jsonInputs, blobInputs);
    try {
      const pdf = document.exportPdf();
      const thumbnails = Array.from({ length: document.pageCount }, (_, page) =>
        document.exportPng(2.0, PageRange.single(page)),
      );
    } finally {
      document.dispose();
    }
    ```

    `CompiledDocument` implements `Symbol.dispose`, so `using document = template.compile(...)` releases it for you. TypeScript needs `ESNext.Disposable` in the `lib` of your `tsconfig.json` for that; the Vite `react-ts` scaffold ships `"lib": ["ES2023", "DOM"]` and reports `Cannot find global type 'Disposable'` until you add it.
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="C#">
    ```csharp
    using Oicana.Config;

    using var document = template.Compile(
        jsonInputs,
        blobInputs,
        new CompilationOptions(CompilationMode.Production));

    var pdf = document.ExportPdf();
    var thumbnails = Enumerable
        .Range(0, document.PageCount)
        .Select(page => document.ExportPng(2.0f, PageRange.Single(page)))
        .ToList();
    ```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Java">
    ```java
    import com.oicana.CompiledDocument;
    import com.oicana.PageRange;

    try (CompiledDocument document = template.compile(jsonInputs, blobInputs)) {
        byte[] pdf = document.exportPdf();

        for (int page = 0; page < document.pageCount(); page++) {
            byte[] thumbnail = document.exportPng(2.0f, PageRange.single(page));
        }
    }
    ```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="TS (Node.js)">
    ```typescript
    import { PageRange, Template } from '@oicana/node';

    using document = await template.compileAsync(jsonInputs, blobInputs);

    const pdf = document.exportPdf();
    const thumbnails = Array.from({ length: document.pageCount }, (_, page) =>
      document.exportPng(2.0, PageRange.single(page)),
    );
    ```

    `using` frees the document at the end of the scope. It is TypeScript syntax here: `tsc` compiles it down for you, but plain JavaScript needs Node 24, so call `document.dispose()` in a `finally` block if you are not compiling through TypeScript. See the [Node.js async guide](/docs/guides/nodejs-async/) for when to prefer the `Async` variants.
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="PHP">
    ```php
    use Oicana\PageRange;

    $document = $template->compile(jsonInputs: $jsonInputs);
    try {
        $pdf = $document->exportPdf();

        for ($page = 0; $page < $document->pageCount(); $page++) {
            $thumbnail = $document->exportPng(2.0, PageRange::single($page));
        }
    } finally {
        $document->close();
    }
    ```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Python">
    ```python
    from oicana import PageRange

    with template.compile(json_inputs=json_inputs) as document:
        pdf = document.export_pdf()
        thumbnails = [
            document.export_png(2.0, pages=PageRange.single(page))
            for page in range(len(document.pages))
        ]
    ```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Rust">
    ```rust
    use oicana::export::pages::PageRange;
    use oicana::export::pdf::export_pdf;
    use oicana::export::png::export_png;

    let result = template.compile(inputs)?;

    let pdf = export_pdf(
        &result.document,
        &template,
        template.manifest().pdf_standards(),
        template.manifest().pdf_tagged(),
        None,
    )?;

    let cover = export_png(&result.document, 2.0, Some(&PageRange::single(0)))?;
    ```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>
